docRequirement: scheduled-tasks.md:102 — "A `loop.md` file replaces the built-in maintenance prompt with your own instructions." It is a single default prompt for bare `/loop`, ignored when a prompt is supplied on the command line; resolved project-first (`.claude/loop.md`) then user (`~/.claude/loop.md`) (:108-:109), re-read so "Edits to loop.md take effect on the next iteration" and "content beyond 25,000 bytes is truncated" (:120); when neither file exists the loop must fall back to the built-in maintenance prompt, whose scope :82-:88 fixes in order — continue unfinished work, tend the branch's PR (review comments, failed CI, merge conflicts), then cleanup passes — with no new initiatives and irreversible actions only when the transcript already authorized them.
current: No reader, no constant, no entry point. (1) `grep -rain -e 'loop\.md' -e 'loopMd' -e 'LOOP_MD' packages/*/src apps/*/src apps/electron/resources` returns seven hits: five are comment citations of the unrelated page `agent-sdk/agent-loop.md` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:866, :956; packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:43; packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/dont-ask-mode.test.ts:5; packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/accept-edits-scope.test.ts:10) and two are an @path import-cycle fixture that merely reuses the filename (packages/shared/src/prompts/__tests__/system.test.ts:351-352 writes `AGENTS.md` containing `@loop.md` and a `loop.md` containing `@AGENTS.md`). (2) `grep -rain -e 'maintenance prompt' -e 'maintenancePrompt' -e 'ScheduleWakeup' packages/*/src apps/*/src` returns zero — no built-in maintenance prompt and no self-paced wakeup tool. (3) There is no `/loop` entry point: the bundled tier holds exactly two slugs (apps/electron/resources/skills/plugin-creator, apps/electron/resources/skills/skill-creator, enumerated at runtime by `bundledSkillSlugs`, packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:41-48), and the model-facing command allowlist is two entries — `const ALLOWED_SLASH_COMMANDS = new Set(['compact', 'help'])`, packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/slash-command.ts:10. Every scheduled task therefore carries a literal prompt captured at create time (cron-store.ts:229-241) — there is no default-prompt path for a task created without one, and nothing re-resolves a prompt at fire time.
divergence: Not a wrong key or a wrong path — the entire default-prompt mechanism is absent. Three distinct missing pieces: (a) no resolver for a `loop.md` at either scope, so the fork's rebranded paths (`<project>/.nessy-agent/loop.md`, `<CONFIG_DIR>/loop.md` = `~/.nessy-agent/loop.md`) are inert files; (b) no built-in maintenance prompt constant to fall back to (:82-:88), so there is nothing for `loop.md` to replace; (c) no bare-`/loop` entry point to default, because the bundled tier ships no `loop` slug and the slash-command allowlist is compact/help. Consequence verified separately from the identifier: because `SessionCronService.flush` (session-cron-service.ts:174-187) delivers `record.prompt` as stored, even a hypothetical resolver called at CronCreate time would freeze the text and still violate :120's re-read-on-next-iteration. The 25,000-byte truncation has no analogue either (the only byte cap in the prompts layer is `MAX_OUTPUT_STYLE_BYTES = 32 * 1024`, packages/shared/src/prompts/output-styles.ts:18).

change.what: New file. `MAX_LOOP_MD_BYTES = 25_000` (:120). `BUILTIN_LOOP_MAINTENANCE_PROMPT` is the :82-:88 text in the documented order (continue unfinished conversation work; tend the current branch's PR — review comments, failed CI runs, merge conflicts; cleanup passes such as bug hunts or simplification when nothing else is pending) plus the :88 guard (no new initiatives outside that scope; irreversible actions such as pushing or deleting only when they continue something the transcript already authorized) — paraphrased, not copied from a proprietary bundle, per AGENTS.md's prompt-text rule. `resolveLoopPrompt(projectDir: string, configDir = CONFIG_DIR): { prompt: string; source: 'project' | 'user' | 'builtin'; truncated: boolean }` reads `join(projectDir, NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR, 'loop.md')` first, then `join(configDir, 'loop.md')`, first hit wins (:104, :108); truncates the content at 25 000 BYTES (Buffer.byteLength, not string length); returns the builtin when neither exists. Reuse `NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR` from packages/shared/src/projects/nessy-agent-layout.ts:12 and `CONFIG_DIR` from packages/shared/src/config/paths.ts:21 — do not hand-join `.nessy-agent` or a home path.

userImpact: Latent but reachable in one keystroke. Today a user typing `/loop` gets no command: the bundled tier offers only plugin-creator and skill-creator (apps/electron/resources/skills), and the agent-callable allowlist is `/compact` and `/help` (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/slash-command.ts:10), so the text reaches the model as prose and whatever it improvises is not a scheduled loop. A user who ports a repo from Claude Code carrying `.claude/loop.md`, or who writes `.nessy-agent/loop.md` after reading the page, gets no read, no fallback and no error — the file is silently inert, which is the worst of the three outcomes because it looks configured. What still works is scheduling itself: asking in natural language reaches `CronCreate` and fires correctly (cron-tools.ts:47, session-cron-service.ts:124), so the loss is the one-token entry point and its per-project customization, not the scheduler.
